title: Credit Where Credit Is Due: Contrastive Attribution Topology Search for Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.29292v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: An LLM multi-agent system (MAS) is only as good as the agents it chooses to trust: its accuracy and cost hinge on its topology, meaning which agents are included and how they communicate. A single task score, however, does not reveal which agents help or hinder performance. We propose Contrastive Attribution Topology Search (CATS), which searches for compact teams within a fixed supergraph of specialized agents. An LLM attributer compares execution traces across candidate topologies and assigns credit to individual agents. CATS uses these credits to update supergraph edges while progressively pruning weak edges and agents, yielding a small team for deployment. With small open-weight models and matched candidate evaluations, CATS improves mean accuracy on BigCodeBench by 5.3 percentage points over score-only heuristic search while using 54\% fewer deployment tokens. translated_title: 功归其人：面向多智能体系统的对比归因拓扑搜索
translated_abstract: LLM多智能体系统（MAS）的好坏取决于它选择信任的智能体：其准确性和成本取决于其拓扑结构，即包含哪些智能体以及它们之间如何通信。然而，单一的任务分数无法揭示哪些智能体在帮助或阻碍性能。我们提出了对比归因拓扑搜索（CATS），它在固定的专业化智能体超图内搜索紧凑的团队。一个LLM归因器对比候选拓扑之间的执行轨迹，并为各个智能体分配功劳。CATS利用这些功劳更新超图的边，同时逐步剪除弱边和弱智能体，最终产生一个用于部署的小型团队。在使用小型开源权重模型和匹配的候选评估条件下，CATS在BigCodeBench上比仅基于分数的启发式搜索平均准确率提升了5.3个百分点，同时部署token使用量减少了54%。在MBPP上，CATS以更少的token达到了与最强基线相当的性能。
tldr: CATS方法让LLM归因器通过对比不同候选拓扑的执行轨迹为各智能体精准分配功劳，从而在智能体超图中自动搜索并剪枝出更小更优的多智能体团队，在提升准确率的同时显著降低部署成本。
en_tdlr: CATS employs an LLM attributer to compare execution traces across candidate topologies and assign credit to individual agents, enabling automatic search and pruning of compact multi-agent teams from a supergraph that improve accuracy while significantly reducing deployment token costs.
